info.title: Vulnix API
info.description: The public Vulnix API. Every operation here is reachable with an API token created in Console -> API -> Tokens; see /api/authentication in the docs. There is no version segment in the path - see /api/conventions for why.

post.description:
Marks the first-run WelcomeTour done for the caller's org. Any org
member can complete it (not just an admin) - unlike `PATCH /org`'s
profile fields, this doesn't change anything another admin would need
to gate, and requiring an admin role here would strand a non-admin
invited into a brand-new org with the modal reopening on every visit.

post.summary: Auto Verify Domain Via Dns Connection
post.description:
"Add record automatically" (Domain Detail's DNS tab) - uses the
org's already-connected Vercel/Cloudflare account to create the
verification TXT record via the provider's own API, then immediately
re-runs the same live DNS check `POST /domains/{domain_id}/verify`
uses, so a single click both creates the record and confirms it
(rather than the caller needing a second manual "now click Verify").

get.description:
Story 3.6: every Run belonging to the caller's org, most-recent-first,
each with a Scope target-value summary for display.

Story 4.4 AC #3: side-by-side Findings comparison between two Runs -
registered before `/runs/{run_id}` so this literal path isn't shadowed
by the parameterized route. Code review: role gate matches `GET /runs`/
`GET /runs/{run_id}` (both `admin`-gated, Story 3.6) rather than the
Findings routes' broader `analyst` tier - the Reports UI itself fetches
`GET /runs` to build its list, so gating this any looser would grant an
analyst an API they could never actually reach through the UI.

Response Get Run Runs  Run Id  Get

get.description:
Story 4.7 AC #2/#5/#6: role gate matches `/findings` (`analyst`, not
`/runs/{run_id}`'s `admin`) - Agent Trace is a read-only investigative
view at the same access level as Findings. `RunService.get_run` 404s
for a missing/foreign-org run_id (AD-1) before the trace is even
queried, same tenant-isolation-via-explicit-lookup pattern as every
other `/runs/{run_id}/*` route. An empty `nodes` list (no ingestible
trace) is a valid 200, not a 404 - AC #5's honest empty state.

schema.title: Response Get Run Agent Trace Runs  Run Id  Agent Trace Get

get.description:
Follow-up (2026-08-20): the Phase Timeline previously only ever
rendered while a Run was still live, streamed straight off
`run-events:{run_id}` (Story 3.4) - a terminal Run's detail page never
read that stream at all, so a failed/stopped/finished Run's task
history vanished the moment the SSE connection closed, even though the
same real events were already sitting in Redis. Same
tenant-isolation-via-explicit-lookup pattern as `/agent-trace` above:
`RunService.get_run` 404s for a missing/foreign-org run_id before the
stream is read. Reduces every `phase_update` entry down to one final
state per task (last status wins), in first-seen order - the same
reduction `applyRunEvent` does client-side while a Run is live, just
replayed here from the whole stream instead of folded incrementally.
An empty `phases` list (stream expired past its 7-day TTL, or no
todos were ever created) is a valid 200, not a 404 - same honest-empty
precedent as Agent Trace.

get.description:
Story 4.8 AC #2/#7: every Finding belonging to this Run - gated at
`admin` to match this page's own `GET /runs/{run_id}` (not `analyst`
like the standalone `/findings`/`/runs/{run_id}/agent-trace` routes -
this route is only ever reached from the Run detail page, which
itself requires admin; see Story 4.8 Dev Notes on the pre-existing
role-gate inconsistency this story doesn't resolve). `RunService.get_run`
404s for a missing/foreign-org run_id first (AD-1), same
tenant-isolation-via-explicit-lookup pattern as `get_run_agent_trace`.
An empty result is a valid 200, not a 404.

schema.title: Response Stop Run Runs  Run Id  Stop Post

get.description:
Client-facing live event stream (Story 3.4 AC #1/#2). Same access
level as `GET /runs/{run_id}` - no new RBAC. Existence/org-scoping is
checked once, synchronously, before entering the streaming loop (Task
3, Subtask 3.3) - `RunService.get_run` raises `RunNotFound` (404) for a
missing or cross-org `run_id`, handled by the shared `DomainError`
exception handler exactly like every other route.

Story 4.5: replaces the flat, non-range-aware KPI computation with
`DashboardService`'s full `?range=7d|30d|90d` response (matching
app.vulnix.dev's own `GET /api/dashboard/overview` field shapes, see
docs/Vulnix_Hosted_Product_Analysis.md #3.3) - Security Score (+ delta),
Open Issues, Issues Found, Fix Rate, Pentests, the
severity-breakdown donut, and the issues-over-time/open-vs-fixed/MTTR
time series. `require_auth` (not `require_role`) is preserved - every
org member, any role, can view their own org's dashboard.

schema.title: Response Dashboard Overview Dashboard Overview Get

get.description:
Story 4.3 AC #1/#6: every Finding belonging to the caller's org,
optionally narrowed by `status`/`severity`, plus a severity breakdown
of exactly that returned list (code review 2026-07-21: previously
hard-coded to an all-time "open" count, which silently stopped
matching the list once a filter was applied and dropped the "info"
severity - now computed from `findings` itself, so it always
summarizes "the list above it" per AC #1).

Also carries each finding's real `repository_id` (see
`_resolve_repository_ids`) alongside the `domain_id` `_finding_dict`
already exposes - together these back the Issues screen's
Repositories/Domains filters, which used to be permanently-disabled
placeholders from before either asset type existed.

Story 4.3 AC #2/#6: a single Finding's full detail - 404s for a
missing or cross-org finding_id (AD-1), same shape either way (see
`FindingNotFound`).

Story 5.3: also returns `validate_fix_attempts` (newest-first) so the
client sees the latest Validate-Fix outcome without a separate route -
`_finding_dict` itself is untouched so `list_findings`/the SARIF-
comparison call sites keep their existing (attempt-history-free) shape.

schema.title: Response Update Finding Findings  Finding Id  Patch

get.description:
Story 5.4 AC #5: PDF export of the Finding Timeline (detection event +
every Validate-Fix attempt, chronological). Gated `analyst` - matching
`get_finding`'s own gate, not `get_run_report`'s stricter `admin` gate -
a single Finding's own timeline is data the caller already has full
access to via `GET /findings/{finding_id}`. PDF is the only format this
AC asks for, so no `format` query param/branching.

Free-trial teaser gating: this renders straight from the `Finding`
entity, bypassing `_finding_dict`'s redaction - so a locked
critical/high finding (see `_finding_dict`) must be refused here too,
or a trial org could recover the withheld detail as a PDF.

get.description:
Live event stream for a PR review, mirroring `stream_run_events`
(Story 3.4) exactly - `invoke_engine`'s poll loop is the one shared
Activity behind both `PentestRunWorkflow` and `PRReviewWorkflow`, and it
publishes to `run-events:{run_id}` keyed by whatever `sandbox.run_id` it
was given, which for a PR review IS the pr_review_id (same "run_id XOR
pr_review_id" shared-activity precedent as `capture_evidence`'s
`entity_kind` dispatch) - so `phase_update`/`cost_update`/`finding`/`log`
events already flow for PR reviews with zero worker-side changes; this
route just needed to exist on the read side. Access level matches every
other PR-review route (`require_role("analyst")`), not the run route's
`admin` gate - Story 6.3/6.4/6.5's own established PR-review role.

post.description:
Story 5.1 AC #1/#2/#4/#5/#6: creates a `ValidateFixAttempt` and starts
its `ValidateFixWorkflow`, gated at `analyst` to match this route's
`/findings/*` siblings (not `admin` like `/scopes/{scope_id}/runs` -
Validate-Fix is triggered from the same Finding Detail page every
analyst-level user can already reach).

post.description:
Fix-PR feature: opens a real GitHub Pull Request applying this
Whitebox Finding's engine-derived code fix. Gated `admin` (unlike this
route's `/findings/*` siblings, gated `analyst`) since this is a
real, visible write against the client's own connected repository -
a materially bigger action than triaging/re-testing a finding.
